sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 (2011)
cleanIntro: The Northwest Explorer is T/C's open-ignition swing-block rifle: the trigger guard pivots forward to drop the breech block, and it fires a Number 11 percussion cap sitting on a nipple threaded into the breech plug. That nipple comes out for cleaning, which is the main thing separating this rifle's maintenance from the 209-primer Omega it otherwise resembles. Every step below is quoted from the Northwest Explorer's own manual.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unprimed and uncharged
steps.action: Settle this before anything else. There is no chamber to inspect on a muzzleloader — the verification is the sequence below.
steps.caution: Never attempt to clean or disassemble a charged or capped muzzleloader.
steps.quote: Make sure that the firearm is unprimed and uncharged.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Takedown of the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloading Rifle — p.39

steps.title: Pivot the trigger guard forward to expose the nipple
steps.action: Swing the trigger guard forward and the breech block drops, bringing the nipple in the breech plug into view. Note what the manual says is exposed here — a nipple, not a primer pocket. That is the tell that you are on the right rifle.
steps.quote: Lower the swinging breech block to open the action by pivoting the trigger guard forward. This will expose the nipple in the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Takedown of the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloading Rifle — p.39

steps.title: Check for a cap, then sight the ignition fire channel
steps.action: Confirm no percussion cap is seated on the nipple, then hold the muzzle to a light and look through the ignition fire channel from the breech end. Daylight through the channel is the proof.
steps.quote: Make sure there is no cap seated. Next, holding the muzzle up to the light, look through the ignition fire channel to make sure you can see through it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Takedown of the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloading Rifle — p.39
steps.warn: No light through the channel means charged or obstructed. Stop and unload.

steps.title: If it is charged, uncap it and pull the charge
steps.action: Open the action, confirm the rifle is uncapped, then take the breech plug out and stand the muzzle up so the powder falls clear. The bullet gets pushed out afterwards with the ramrod and the extended super jag.
steps.quote: Open the action and make sure that the firearm is uncapped.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Unloading a Charge from the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloader — p.32

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Pull the ramrod out of the thimbles and set it aside before the barreled action leaves the stock.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod from the thimbles.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Takedown of the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloading Rifle — p.39

steps.title: Close the breech and back out both stock screws
steps.action: Close the swinging breech, then take out the front and rear stock/lug assembly screws. Both turn counter-clockwise as viewed from the bottom of the rifle.
steps.quote: Close the swinging breech and remove both the front and rear stock/lug assembly screws by turning them counter clockwise.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Takedown of the T/C Northwest Explorer Muzzleloading Rifle — p.39

steps.title: Lift the barrel and action out of the stock
steps.action: With both screws out, the barreled action comes up out of the stock. That is the rifle in its two groups — barrel and action, and stock.
steps.quote: The barrel/action assembly may now be lifted out of the stock.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Disassembly — p.40

steps.title: Unscrew the breech plug
steps.action: Open the breech, fit the wrench, and turn counter-clockwise. Expect resistance at the start as the gas seal breaks. If the barrel turns in your hand, clamp the barrel lug in a vise or a crescent wrench.
steps.quote: Open the breech, and insert the breech plug wrench onto the breech plug. Turn counter clockwise to unscrew the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Disassembly — p.40

steps.title: Run the bore
steps.action: Jag on the ramrod, patch soaked in black-powder solvent, up and down the bore until the patches stop coming out fouled, then dry patches until the bore is dry.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive, not just dirty. A bore left overnight uncleaned can be pitted by morning. Follow the wet patches with dry ones until the bore is dry.
steps.quote: Use the cleaning jag that was provided with the T/C Northwest Explorer, and a cleaning patch saturated with a bore cleaner like Thompson/Center’s No.13™ Solvent. Run the saturated patch up and down the bore a few times - to remove the fouling
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Field Cleaning — p.35

steps.title: Take the nipple out and clean it
steps.action: This is the step that belongs to this rifle and not to the Omega. The nipple unthreads from the breech plug for cleaning or replacement — the manual calls for a 7/16 inch open end wrench and a T/C nipple wrench.
steps.quote: The nipple can be removed from the breech plug for cleaning or replacement as needed
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Thorough Cleaning — p.37
steps.warn: Use only Thompson/Center nipples. Be certain the threads are not cross-threaded and the nipple is snug before loading and firing.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel clear, barreled action out of the stock, plug out, nipple serviced, bore clean. That is routine maintenance on the Northwest Explorer. The manual's thorough cleaning and full takedown detail is in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: If the T/C Northwest Explorer muzzleloader has become very dirty due to extensive firing, the shooter may need to disassemble the rifle further than just removing the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Thorough Cleaning — p.38

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug and both thread sets
deepSteps.action: Clean the fouling off the plug, then get a stiff brush and solvent into the barrel's own breech threads. Dry both, then anti-seize both — that is what keeps the plug removable next season.
deepSteps.quote: Once removed, the breech plug should be scrubbed free of fouling and then the threads should be lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant like T/C's Super Lube, before reinstallation.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
deepSteps.action: Stand the muzzle in hot soapy water and pump a wet patch on the jag from the breech end. The barrel siphons the water through and the fouling comes with it.
deepSteps.caution: Dry the bore completely before oiling. Water left in a black-powder barrel rusts fast.
deepSteps.quote: Pump the ramrod and patch up and down in the barrel. This will draw water into the barrel and flush out the fouling.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Wipe out the frame assembly
deepSteps.action: Powder residue gets into the frame every time the breech swings open. Clear it out, dry the parts and give them a light oil — light, because heavy oil congeals in cold weather and can slow or stop the hammer fall.
deepSteps.quote: Thoroughly wipe any powder residue from the frame assembly. Dry the parts thoroughly and lubricate them lightly to prevent rust and corrosion.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Seat the plug to snug
deepSteps.action: Thread the plug in clockwise with the wrench and stop at snug. T/C gives a hand test instead of a torque figure, and the test is unambiguous once you have felt it.
deepSteps.caution: Improper type or installation of breech plugs can cause injury and damage to property.
deepSteps.quote: “Snug” is defined as being as tight as you can turn it into the barrel by using the breech plug wrench and turning it clockwise, while holding the barrel in your hand.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C® Northwest Explorer™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:T/C NWExPLORERML_083011, P/N 00084001 — Disassembly — p.40

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag until they come out clean
Dry patches until the bore is dry
Light lubricant on the bore once completely dry

cleaning.name: Ignition
tasks: Remove the nipple from the breech plug with a 7/16 inch open end wrench and a T/C nipple wrench
Clean the nipple and the matching threads in the breech plug
Confirm the nipple is a Thompson/Center part and threads in cleanly and snug
Moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin within the breech block

cleaning.name: Breech plug and frame
tasks: Scrub the plug free of fouling
Stiff brush and solvent through the barrel's breech threads, then dry
Anti-seize on both the plug threads and the barrel threads
Wipe all powder residue out of the frame assembly and dry it

reassembly: Thread the cleaned nipple back into the breech plug until snug
Anti-seize the plug threads and the barrel's breech threads
Thread the breech plug in clockwise until snug, checking it is not cross-threaded
Lower the barreled action into the stock
Fit and tighten both stock/lug assembly screws
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle uncapped and uncharged, swing the trigger guard through its travel and check the trigger and hammer mechanism for proper function before loading and firing.
